ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The A gene of Arabidopsis thaliana is located on chromosome 1 and affects the exchange frequency of chromosomes during meiosis; the a gene has no such function. The B gene is located on chromosome 5 and causes the four pollen grains from the same pollen mother cell to separate; the b gene has no such function. Plant A (AaBB) and plant B (AAbb) were used as parents for a hybridization experiment, and the required plant C (aabb) was obtained in F2. Before hybridization, fluorescent protein genes C and R were integrated on chromosome 1 of B. After two generations, C obtained the C and R genes (Figure 2). Pollen grains carrying the C and R genes can respectively show blue and red fluorescence. When the pollen mother cells of C undergo meiosis, if only one exchange occurs between the C and R gene loci on the chromosome, what colors will the four pollen grains produced respectively show?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: Blue, red, superimposed color of blue and red, colorless

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The A gene of Arabidopsis thaliana is located on chromosome 1 and affects the exchange frequency of chromosomes during meiosis; the a gene has no such function. The B gene is located on chromosome 5 and causes the four pollen grains from the same pollen mother cell to separate; the b gene has no such function. Plant A (AaBB) and plant B (AAbb) were used as parents for a hybridization experiment, and the required plant C (aabb) was obtained in F2. Before hybridization, fluorescent protein genes C and R were integrated on chromosome 1 of B. After two generations, C obtained the C and R genes (Figure 2). Pollen grains carrying the C and R genes can respectively show blue and red fluorescence. When the pollen mother cells of C undergo meiosis, if only one exchange occurs between the C and R gene loci on the chromosome, what colors will the four pollen grains produced respectively show?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Blue, red, superimposed color of blue and red, colorless
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In Figure 2, on the two homologous chromosomes of chromosome 1 of plant C, both homologous chromosomes are marked with a; fluorescent protein gene C is located on one chromosome 1, and fluorescent protein gene R is located on the other homologous chromosome, indicating that C and R are arranged in trans. The stem states that pollen grains carrying C show blue fluorescence, and pollen grains carrying R show red fluorescence. Reasoning: When the pollen mother cells of C undergo meiosis, if only one exchange occurs between the C and R gene loci, then among the four chromatids, two retain the parental type and respectively carry only C or only R; the other two are recombinant types and respectively carry both C and R or carry neither. Therefore, the colors corresponding to the four pollen grains are: the one carrying only C is blue, the one carrying only R is red, the one carrying both C and R is the superimposed color of blue and red, and the one carrying neither C nor R is colorless.
